structuralDecisions.decision: Implement both endpoints inside apps/mock-api/server.js following the exact readJSON/writeJSON + flat-handler pattern already used by items, orders, and reagent-sites. No new package, module, class, or Clean Architecture layering is introduced.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Verified server.js directly: readItems/readOrders/readReagentSites and their handlers are structurally identical to what this feature needs for readExpeditions/writeExpeditions. apps/mock-api has no domain/application/adapter split today — introducing one for two endpoints would be inconsistent with every other endpoint in the file and is explicitly outside scope.paths. This matches CLAUDE.md's architect-skip criterion for purely additive work within an established pattern, and repeats the precedent architecture-notes.md already set for reagent-sites-api.
tradeOffs: Carries forward the existing unbounded in-memory JSON reload-per-request cost — acceptable at this app's demo scale, same as every other endpoint.
Defers (again) the cost reagent-sites-api's architecture notes already flagged: a later slice needing a richer Expedition domain model will have to revisit server.js's flat structure.

structuralDecisions.decision: Introduce a new, explicitly named optional-session helper — resolveSessionUserId(req) — that returns the session's user id or null, and never rejects the request. GET /api/expeditions uses this helper; it MUST NOT use requireAuth, and requireAuth MUST NOT be changed to support an optional mode.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This is the one genuinely new structural element in this feature: every existing endpoint is either fully public or fully gated by requireAuth's all-or-nothing contract (missing/invalid token -> 401). GET /api/expeditions needs a third shape — proceed regardless, personalize if possible. Solving this by adding an 'optional' flag to requireAuth would corrupt a contract every other call site already depends on being all-or-nothing. A separate, named function keeps the two contracts impossible to confuse: requireAuth guards; resolveSessionUserId informs.
tradeOffs: Two session-lookup code paths now exist (requireAuth's and resolveSessionUserId's) instead of one — acceptable because they have genuinely different contracts, and the alternative (overloading requireAuth) is worse.
Any future endpoint needing optional auth must reuse resolveSessionUserId rather than reinventing it — noted in developer handoff.

fitness.property: GET /api/expeditions returns 200 for every request regardless of Authorization header content (absent, malformed, expired, or valid), and a valid session's response set equals the shop's seeded expeditions plus exactly that session's own expeditions — never another adventurer's.
fitness.verification: node --test apps/mock-api — qa-engineer asserts: (1) no Authorization header -> 200 with exactly the 3 seeded expeditions; (2) garbage/expired token -> 200 with exactly the 3 seeded expeditions (never 401); (3) Elara's valid session -> seeded + Elara's own, Borin's absent; (4) Borin's valid session -> seeded + Borin's own, Elara's absent.

structuralDecisions.decision: The endpoint-to-endpoint distance check (haversine geodesic distance) is a pure function, geodesicDistanceKm(from, to, radiusKm), colocated in server.js near the other helpers, with AURELIS_RADIUS_KM = 6000 and MIN_EXPEDITION_DISTANCE_KM = 1 as named constants at the top of the file — not inline magic numbers, and not extracted into a separate module or package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md IV forbids magic numbers; naming the constants satisfies that without introducing new structure. Extracting a separate geo-math module or an Expedition domain package now would be premature generalization (design-principles.md #7) against work that doesn't exist yet — apps/mock-api has no domain layer to receive it, and no second caller exists yet. Keeping it a pure function (no I/O, no req/res) means it is trivially unit-testable in isolation from the Express handler, which is what keeps the handler itself under the complexity budget despite combining JSON I/O, auth, and validation.
tradeOffs: If a later slice (e.g. multi-point expeditions, routing) needs richer geo-math, this function will need to move into whatever domain layer that slice introduces — deferred, not eliminated.
No test currently proves the constant is actually used (vs. a hardcoded duplicate) short of code-reviewer's manual check, since apps/mock-api has no magic-number lint rule configured.

fitness.property: geodesicDistanceKm is a standalone, side-effect-free function with no dependency on req/res/fs; AURELIS_RADIUS_KM and MIN_EXPEDITION_DISTANCE_KM are declared as named constants, used by both the handler and directly by tests, never duplicated as literals elsewhere in the expedition-related code.
fitness.verification: Manual review by code-reviewer (apps/mock-api has no magic-number/no-restricted-syntax ESLint rule configured today — same tooling gap reagent-sites-api's architecture-notes.md already recorded); qa-engineer additionally unit-tests geodesicDistanceKm directly with known coordinate pairs to prove it can fail independently of the HTTP layer.

structuralDecisions.decision: POST /api/expeditions MUST construct the persisted record from an explicit allow-list — { id, owner: req.userId, from, to, savedAt } — and MUST NOT spread or copy req.body wholesale into the stored object. owner and savedAt are never read from the request body.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This is the feature's core trust-boundary invariant (AC11, and the security gate's named property: 'POST always stores req.userId as owner, ignoring any owner/userId field the request body supplies'). The existing POST /api/orders handler already destructures named fields rather than spreading req.body, so this follows the codebase's own established safe pattern — it is not a new convention, just the one that must not be skipped here under time pressure.
tradeOffs: Slightly more verbose than `{ ...req.body, id, owner: req.userId }` — that shorthand is explicitly rejected because object key order in a spread does not protect against a later field reordering reintroducing the vulnerability; the allow-list form has no such failure mode.

fitness.property: Submitting a POST body that includes a forged owner or userId field never changes the stored or returned owner from req.userId.
fitness.verification: node --test apps/mock-api — security-reviewer/qa-engineer POST with { from, to, owner: 'shop' } (or another user's id) using Elara's session, assert the stored and returned expedition's owner equals Elara's user id, not the forged value.

structuralDecisions.decision: apps/mock-api/data/expeditions.json stores pre-resolved { from: {lat,lng}, to: {lat,lng} } coordinate pairs for every seeded expedition, copied at seed-authoring time from reagent-sites.json's existing site records. Neither GET nor POST /api/expeditions reads reagent-sites.json at request time; the two data files are not runtime-coupled.
structuralDecisions.rationale: The API contract (per domain-model.md H1, carried into analysis.md) is 'a line and its owner' — two coordinate pairs, not two site-id references. Resolving site-name-to-coordinate once, by hand, when authoring the seed file keeps GET /api/expeditions a single readJSON call (matching every other GET handler's shape) and avoids introducing a foreign-key-style lookup between two otherwise-independent data files for a read-only seed. This also means expeditions-api introduces zero runtime dependency on reagent-sites-api's data file, keeping the two orders' sibling relationship (noted in both analyses) read-only and one-directional at authoring time only.
tradeOffs: If reagent-sites.json's coordinates for Moonwell Spring, Ember Crag, etc. ever change, expeditions.json's seeded coordinates will silently go stale unless someone re-derives them by hand — acceptable for a demo seed file, called out here so it isn't mistaken for a bug later.

structuralDecisions.decision: No CircuitBreaker, ExponentialBackoffStrategy, or network timeout is introduced for this feature, and none is needed: the distance check is synchronous in-memory arithmetic with zero network calls, consistent with the NFR that no request may leave the app's/mock API's own origins.
structuralDecisions.rationale: architecture-guardrails.md #5 only applies to network calls; there are none here. This decision exists to make explicit and testable the NFR that a future contributor must not 'upgrade' the distance check to call an external geocoding/mapping API.

fitness.property: No new outbound HTTP/network client (fetch, axios, a geocoding SDK, etc.) is imported or used anywhere in the expedition-related code added by this feature.
fitness.verification: code-reviewer greps the diff for new require()/import of an HTTP client library in the expedition handlers and helper; absence confirms the check stayed local.

New auth-adjacent helper, deliberately separate from requireAuth so the all-or-nothing and optional contracts can never be confused; placed next to requireAuth/generateToken.
Uses resolveSessionUserId, never requireAuth; placed in its own '============ EXPEDITIONS ENDPOINTS ============' block near /api/reagent-sites.
Gated by requireAuth, mirrors POST /api/orders' req.userId-as-owner pattern with an explicit field allow-list instead of a body spread.

crossings: Identity (mock API session store) — reads req.userId via the existing requireAuth middleware and the new resolveSessionUserId helper; does not change sign-in or session creation.
reagent-sites-api — expeditions.json's seeded coordinates are copied from reagent-sites.json's site records at seed-authoring time only; no runtime read of that file by either new endpoint.
features/reagent-map UI slices (reagent-map-globe, reagent-map-save) — future, not-yet-built consumers of these two endpoints, gated separately by VITE_FEATURE_REAGENT_MAP; out of scope here.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: No Clean Architecture layer boundary applies — apps/mock-api/server.js is a flat, single-file Express app with no domain/application/adapter separation.
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Confirmed by reading server.js directly (loom MCP graph tools were not used — not needed for a single-file app with no directory structure to query). No dependency-direction violation is possible to introduce because there is no inner/outer layer split to violate.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: The new optional-auth helper (resolveSessionUserId) must not be reachable from, or merged into, requireAuth's gating contract.
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Enforced by naming and placement decision above (structuralDecisions #2) rather than by a graph query; verified by reading requireAuth and confirming no shared code path is proposed between it and the new helper.

antiPatternChecks.notes: Considered and rejected extracting an Expedition domain class, a geo-math module, or a shared sites/expeditions linkage now; deferred until a slice actually needs it (structuralDecisions #1, #3, #5).

server.js continues to grow (now six endpoint groups), same as reagent-sites-api's note recorded. Not worsened materially by two more handlers in the established style; refactoring server.js is outside scope.paths for this order.
resolveSessionUserId returns a plain user id or null — callers don't need to know how sessions are stored, same abstraction level requireAuth already exposes.
All changes are additive and localized to server.js plus two new/extended data files; no existing endpoint's behavior changes.

developerHandoffNotes: Add EXPEDITIONS_PATH, readExpeditions(), writeExpeditions() to server.js following readJSON/writeJSON exactly as readItems/readOrders do.

Add AURELIS_RADIUS_KM = 6000 and MIN_EXPEDITION_DISTANCE_KM = 1 as named constants near the top of server.js (not inline literals), and implement geodesicDistanceKm(from, to, radiusKm) as a pure function with no req/res/fs access, so qa-engineer can unit-test it directly against known coordinate pairs.

Add resolveSessionUserId(req) next to requireAuth: reads the Authorization header, looks up sessions.get(token), returns the user id or null — it must never call res.status() or next() itself; it is a plain lookup, not middleware.

GET /api/expeditions: no requireAuth. Call resolveSessionUserId(req); always return the shop's (owner: 'shop') expeditions, plus — only when resolveSessionUserId returned a non-null id — that session's own expeditions filtered by owner === that id.

POST /api/expeditions: behind requireAuth. Validate body.from/body.to as {lat, lng}; call geodesicDistanceKm; reject with 422 naming a zero-length line when distance < MIN_EXPEDITION_DISTANCE_KM. On success, build the stored record as { id, owner: req.userId, from, to, savedAt: new Date().toISOString() } — an explicit allow-list, never a spread of req.body — and return it.

Build apps/mock-api/data/expeditions.json by hand: copy the three seeded expeditions' from/to coordinates out of the current apps/mock-api/data/reagent-sites.json records (Moonwell Spring, Ember Crag, Thornveil Glade, Glimmerdeep Caves, Saltmarsh Cairn, Tidewrack Shoals), plus Elara's (Moonwell Spring → Frostcap Hollow) and Borin's (Ember Crag → Saltmarsh Cairn) expeditions with owner set to their respective user ids. Do not add a runtime read of reagent-sites.json into either handler.
Add Elara and Borin to apps/mock-api/data/users.json matching the existing user record shape exactly (id, email, password, name, createdAt, address).
Add both new endpoints to the startup console.log endpoint list, matching the existing style.
Do not introduce an Expedition class, repository interface, or shared package in this slice — stay inside server.js's existing flat style, per structuralDecisions #1 and #5.
